children: SYDNEY--Australian consumer confidence tumbled to a six-week low last week, weighed down by mounting concerns that the central bank could push through as many as two additional interest-rate hikes before year-end.

Consumer confidence fell 3.0 points over the week to 71.9 points, according to a survey by ANZ Bank and pollster Roy Morgan. The four-week moving average for confidence dropped 0.8 points to 75.2 points.
Meanwhile, weekly inflation expectations rose 0.2 percentage points to 6.3%, while the four-week moving average ticking up 0.1 percentage points to 6.1%, the data showed Tuesday.

The recent release of strong inflation and GDP growth figures has heightened expectations for further interest rates increases by the Reserve Bank of Australia which is set to meet again later this month.
Confidence around current financial conditions was down 7.5 points last week, while the outlook for future financial conditions dipped 2.4 points.
A subindex tracking the appetite for major household purchases also fell, dropping 1.9 points.
The prospect of another RBA rate hike in 2026 may have weighed on sentiment, said Sophia Angala, an economist at ANZ.
Weekly inflation expectations rose to their highest level since early May, when negotiations between the U.S. and Iran stalled, she added.
ANZ expects the RBA to increase the official cash rate by 25 basis points in November.
The weekly ANZ-Roy Morgan Australian consumer confidence rating was based on 1,041 interviews.
